hooks.text: A hundred million dollar Mars orbiter vanished from a simple math mix-up.
NASA lost a spacecraft at Mars because two teams used different units.
Pounds versus newtons caused a one hundred million dollar Mars disaster.

title: The Mars Mistake That Lost an Orbiter
description: Discover how a unit mismatch between pounds and newtons led to the loss of the Mars Climate Orbiter in nineteen ninety-nine.

beats.text: A hundred million dollar Mars orbiter vanished from a simple math mix-up.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Mars Climate Orbiter in flight, 1998

beats.text: Most people assume it was a sudden rocket failure, but the truth hid in software.
beats.visual: Delta II rocket launch carrying Mars Climate Orbiter from Cape Canaveral, 1998
queries: Delta II Mars Climate Orbiter launch

beats.text: Lockheed Martin built the spacecraft to calculate thrusters using pound-force seconds.
beats.visual: Lockheed Martin engineers working on spacecraft assembly, 1998

beats.text: Meanwhile, NASA navigation software expected metric newton-seconds for those exact thrusters.
beats.visual: Jet Propulsion Laboratory mission control room during operations, 1999

beats.text: Because one pound-force equals about 4.45 newtons, the system treated force as twenty-two percent of its actual value.
beats.visual: diagram of Hohmann transfer orbit for Mars missions, 1999

beats.text: Those tiny uncorrected errors accumulated over a nine-month journey across space.
beats.visual: Mars atmosphere limb captured by spacecraft in orbit, 1999

beats.text: On September twenty-third, nineteen ninety-nine, the probe plunged to a lethal altitude of just thirty-five miles.
beats.visual: artist's concept of Mars Global Surveyor in orbit, 1999

beats.text: Navigators spotted discrepancies earlier, but managers dismissed their warnings because proper paperwork was missing.
beats.visual: JPL mission control staff reviewing telemetry data, 1999

beats.text: That fatal refusal to file correct forms is why a hundred million dollar Mars orbiter vanished from a simple math mix-up.
beats.visual: artist's concept of Mars Polar Lander, 1999
